To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the social intelligence of the agent can be enhanced through cross cultural communication.

(a) the social interactions are the key to understand the cultural differences; (b) the cultural differences in the social interactions can be represented by the difference in the communication styles; and (c) the communication styles can be characterized in terms of the social distance between the parties involved.

the cultural differences in communication can be modeled as the difference in social interaction styles and that the social interaction styles can be modeled as a combination of social interaction patterns.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: • The first is the development of the cultural theory of communication.
the following six grand challenges on cross cultural communication: 1) What is the difference in social interactions between cultures?

the following six issues: 1) how to identify the cultural gap in the social interaction between the parties; 2) how to model the culture in the form of social interaction; 3) how to identify social interactions in the cultural context; 4) how to create socially intelligent agents; 5) how to create culturally sensitive agents; 6) how to create agents that are sensitive to cultural changes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“cultural issues are unavoidable and should be taken into account in creating adaptive software agents”.

the grand challenges are to develop the following capabilities for a culturally adaptive socially intelligent agent: (1) to recognize and to understand the culture-specific communication style and its influence in the social interaction, (2) to recognize cultural difference and its influence in social interactions, (3) to recognize the cultural difference in the social interaction and to adjust its behavior accordingly, (4) to recognize the culture-specific social interaction and its influence in human-agent and agent-human communications, (5) to recognize cultural differences in
the grand challenge of cross cultural communication is to create socially intelligent agents that have the capability to communicate with other agents or humans with different cultural background.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cross cultural communication research should be conducted in the context of social interactions.
we have developed an integrated approach for studying cross cultural communication.

the cultural issues are important in the communications conducted among the software agents, and that the cultural differences should be considered as the important factor in the design of the socially intelligent agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cultural differences in communication can be modeled by the difference in the interaction patterns of the parties involved in communications.
the cultural influence in communications is not a simple matter of “translation” or “adaptation” of a message.
cultural differences in human-human communications can be modeled as differences in forms of social interaction.
